claims.head: Like for like: Coyle against Matthews
claims.call: The Blue Jackets’ L2 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Maple Leafs’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Maple Leafs’ second line is Cowan, Matthews and Roslovic.
claims.nums: At home: 46% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 27% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rick Bowness likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Maple Leafs’ second line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Columbus home games this season · 5 games, 56 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Columbus’s L2 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) at home: 46% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ second lines. Matchups, Columbus home games this season, 5 games, 56 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Chris Tanev is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Darren Raddysh has taken his spot beside Jake McCabe.
John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
William Nylander is out (illness), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Marshall Rifai was added to the roster on Oct 12.
Vinni Lettieri was added to the roster on Oct 19 and has played beside Colton Sissons and Gavin McKenna.
Ivan Provorov is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Zach Werenski has taken his spot beside Denton Mateychuk.

CBJ.head: The Blue Jackets should be favored
CBJ.body: Columbus has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, has home-ice advantage and gets Andrae back, while Toronto is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Maple Leafs’ best way in is a power play that gets going.

TOR.head: A steep climb for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Columbus has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, has home-ice advantage and gets Andrae back, while Toronto is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Maple Leafs can still win it if their power play gets going, but a lot has to go their way.
